slot.brief: Four statements about diagonal relationship / reactions of Ca and Mg compounds — e.g. thermal decomposition of CaCO3 vs MgCO3, solubility of sulfates down the group — pick the incorrect one.

stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: CaCO$_3$ is thermally more stable than MgCO$_3$.
Ca(OH)$_2$ is more soluble in water than Mg(OH)$_2$.
CaSO$_4$ is more soluble in water than MgSO$_4$.
Both CaCl$_2$ and MgCl$_2$ are deliquescent in nature.

verdicts.working: Carbonate thermal stability and hydroxide solubility increase down Group 2, so (A) and (B) are true. MgSO₄ is more soluble than CaSO₄, making (C) incorrect. Both chlorides are deliquescent.

working:
Solubility of sulphates of group 2 decreases from Be to Ba. MgSO$_4$ is highly soluble, whereas CaSO$_4$ is sparingly soluble. Thermal stability of carbonates increases down the group (CaCO$_3$ > MgCO$_3$). Solubility of hydroxides increases down the group; Ca(OH)$_2$ is moderately soluble, Mg(OH)$_2$ is sparingly soluble. Both CaCl$_2$ and MgCl$_2$ are deliquescent.

Independent check: Carbonate thermal stability and hydroxide solubility increase down Group 2, so (A) and (B) are true. MgSO₄ is more soluble than CaSO₄, making (C) incorrect. Both chlorides are deliquescent.
solution:
Solubility of Group 2 sulphates decreases down the group; hence MgSO$_4$ is more soluble than CaSO$_4$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the statement that CaSO}_4\text{ is more soluble than MgSO}_4\text{ is incorrect.}$$
